name: Van Cortlandt Golf Course
note: The oldest public golf course in the United States: 'established in 1895 as a nine-hole course and expanded to eighteen holes in 1899' (opened 6 July 1895). Point: the holes north of the lake (OSM outlines 'Van Cortlandt Golf Course' and its unnamed duplicate).

name: Van Cortlandt Golf Course
note: Same course: the four holes south of Van Cortlandt Lake (unnamed OSM outlines that also take in Mosholu); the 1899 enlargement to 18 holes is not separated (estimated).

name: Mosholu Golf Course
note: Nine-hole course in the south-east corner of Van Cortlandt Park, 'built in 1914'. OSM maps it without a name; the point is inside its outline.

name: Pelham Bay & Split Rock Golf Course
note: 'The Pelham Bay Golf Course opened in 1901, followed by the Split Rock Golf Course in 1935.' One OSM outline for both: features take the year of the nearer point. Pelham Bay course = the eastern half toward Shore Road (position of the split ESTIMATED).

name: Pelham Bay & Split Rock Golf Course
note: Split Rock Golf Course, John van Kleek, opened June 1935 with the rebuilt Pelham course ('The golf courses were reopened in June 1935'): the western half toward the Hutchinson River marshes and Split Rock (position of the split ESTIMATED).

name: Forest Park Golf Course
note: 'A nine-hole golf course opened in 1901 ... a clubhouse and another nine holes were added in 1905.' The 1905 holes are not separated (estimated).

name: Dyker Beach Golf Course
note: ESTIMATED. Golf on the Dyker Meadow from the late 1890s: the Dyker Meadow company 'leased the land to both the Dyker Golf Club and Marine and Field Club, who used the Dyker Heights Club House, built in 1898, as their golf club house'; 'second oldest in New York City, behind Van Cortlandt'. The city course took its present extent with the parcels of 1924-27 and 1934 and the fill begun in 1918: later holes are not separated.

name: Richmond County Country Club
note: Club founded 1888, golf from 1894; 'In 1897, RCCC moved to its present location in Dongan Hills'.

name: Towers Country Club
note: Unnamed in OSM (the course around North Shore Towers, Glen Oaks). 'In 1923, the Glen Oaks Golf Club was built'; the towers replaced part of the course by 1971 and the remaining holes were rearranged: today's layout is younger than 1923 (ESTIMATED).

name: Clearview Park
note: Clearview Park Golf Course (OSM name 'Clearview Park'): opened 1925 as the private Clearview Golf and Yacht Club (Willie Tucker); bought by the city 25 June 1931 (NYC Parks, read through a search result: the site refuses automated requests).

name: South Shore Golf Course
note: 'South Shore Golf Course, built in 1927' (Staten Island Chamber of Commerce) as a private country club; city course later. Other listings say 1929.

name: Douglaston Golf Course
note: ESTIMATED. Built as the North Hills Country Club, designed by Willie Tucker in 1925 (Bayside Historical Society); the opening year 1927 is not verified in a source read here. City course since the early 1960s (Parks acquisition date 7 Sep 1962).

name: Silver Lake Golf Course
note: 'In 1928 the land was converted to a golf course ... The golf course itself was completed in 1929' (on the former Marine Cemetery).

name: La Tourette Golf Course
note: 'The first nine holes, designed by David L. Rees, opened in 1929. In 1935, John Van Kleek designed nine new holes and redesigned the original nine.' The 1935 holes are not separated (estimated).

name: Kissena Golf Course
note: 'Designed by John Van Kleek, the Kissena Park golf course opened in 1935' (NYSGA; some listings say 1934).

name: Jacob Riis Park Golf Course
note: 'The park's pitch and putt golf course was opened on May 14, 1938.'

name: Alley Pond Golf Center
note: ESTIMATED: driving range east of the Northern Boulevard bridge over Alley Creek; 'The golf center has operated since the 1950s'.

name: Marine Park Golf Course
note: 'The 210-acre golf course opened in 1963' (Robert Trent Jones, on Jamaica Bay fill).

name: Flushing Meadows Golf Center
note: ESTIMATED: pitch-and-putt and miniature golf at the north end of Meadow Lake, on 1964-65 World's Fair ground; dated to the park's return to the city in June 1967. The centre's own opening year was not found.

name: Bally's Golf Links at Ferry Point
note: Jack Nicklaus course on the former landfill: 'the golf course, which opened in 2015' (as Trump Golf Links at Ferry Point; renamed 2023).

name: Shady Rest Country Club
note: 'In 1900, the Westfield Country Club was organized as a golf club. It leased the land ..., built a 9-hole golf course'; 'opened the Shady Rest Country Club on July 28, 1921'; public course since 1964.

name: Canoe Brook Country Club
note: 'founded in 1901'; 'The first nine holes opened for play in 1902; the second nine in 1905.' One outline holds both courses (the North and South Course outlines lie inside it and carry no row of their own); the second course is not dated in the article: the whole club from 1902 (ESTIMATED for the later holes).

name: Baltusrol Golf Course
note: 'The club's original 9-hole course was designed by George Hunter in 1895 and expanded to 18 holes in 1898'; today's Upper and Lower courses 'officially opened for play in June 1922' (not separated).

name: Galloping Hill Golf Course
note: Infobox: established 1928 (Union County's public course, Willard G. Wilkinson).

name: Weequahic Golf Course
note: 'the first nine holes were designed in 1913 by George Low, with the course opening for play in 1914' (the oldest public course in New Jersey; later holes not separated).

name: Essex County Country Club
note: ESTIMATED: 'In 1916, A.W. Tillinghast designed a new 18-hole course, called the "Upper Course," on a 180 acres site on top of First Mountain, a few miles away from the original course' (club founded 1887); the opening year of that course is not in the article.

name: Upper Montclair Country Club
note: 'The original 18-hole golf course and a new clubhouse opened in 1928' (club established 1901; rebuilt to 27 holes in the 1950s).

name: East Orange Golf Course
note: ESTIMATED: Tom Bendelow's list of designs gives 'East Orange GC ... 1923 ... East Orange, New Jersey'; the opening year was not checked.

name: Liberty National Golf Club
note: Infobox: established 2006 (on a former oil terminal).

name: Bayonne Golf Club
note: Wikidata inception (P571) 2006; not checked against a second source.

name: The Ridgewood Country Club
note: 'founded in 1890 in neighboring Ho-Ho-Kus, but has been at its current location since 1926'; course by A. W. Tillinghast, 1929 (infobox: established 1929).

name: White Beeches Golf and Country Club
note: 'The course was built in 1918 and designed by Walter Travis.'

name: Knickerbocker Country Club
note: Donald Ross's list of courses: 'Knickerbocker Country Club (1914), Tenafly'.

name: Montclair Golf Club
note: ESTIMATED lower bound: Donald Ross's list of courses gives 'Montclair Golf Club (1920), West Orange'; the club is older and may have played on this ground before (not checked).

name: Preakness Valley Golf Course
note: ESTIMATED lower bound: 'Made public in 1931, this full service course is considered the first public golf course in Passaic County' — the private course the county took over is older (year not found).

name: Dellwood Country Club
note: Adolph Zukor's Mountain View Farm: A. W. Tillinghast's 'eighteen-hole golf course on the property, which opened in 1920'; a club since 1936 (Dellwood from 1948, Paramount Country Club today).

name: Rockland Country Club
note: 'The club was incorporated in 1906 and commissioned Henry Stark to design a 9-hole course that was ready the following year'; 'an entirely new golf course that opened in 1930' (not separated).

name: Sleepy Hollow Country Club
note: 'The country club was incorporated on May 11, 1911'; 'the club had Charles B. Macdonald and Seth Raynor design the first golf course in 1911'.

name: Trump National Golf Club Westchester
note: 'In 1922, Devereux Emmet designed a course ... with eighteen holes, and thus Briarcliff Country Club was founded that year'; rebuilt for 'its 2002 reopening' (the closure before it is not shown).

name: The Saint Andrew's Golf Club
note: 'The current site, the club's home since 1897' (club founded 1888 in Yonkers).

name: Wykagyl Golf Club
note: 'Lawrence Van Etten ... laid out the original golf course when the club moved to New Rochelle in 1905.'

name: Scarsdale Country Club
note: Scarsdale Golf Club, Hartsdale: 'The club contains the Scarsdale Golf Course, founded in 1898'.

name: Westchester Country Club
note: 'Founded in 1922 as a destination for sportsmen' (Walter Travis's courses).

name: Rye Golf Club
note: 'originally organized on July 1, 1921, as the Rye Country Club' (course by Devereux Emmet, 1921).

name: Quaker Ridge Golf Club
note: 'The club was formed ... in 1916 by a group of businessmen who had acquired the land a year earlier from a smaller, financially strained club. The course was completed in 1918'.

name: Winged Foot Golf Club
note: 'The club was founded in 1921 ... and opened in June 1923.'

name: Pelham Country Club
note: Infobox: established 1921 (Devereux Emmet; Emmet's own list of courses in his article says 1908 for the club).

name: Bedford Golf and Tennis Club
note: Devereux Emmet's list of courses: 'Bedford Golf and Tennis Club Bedford, New York, 1891' (the club's year; the present holes are not dated).

name: Harrison Meadows Country Club
note: 'Green Meadow Club, Rye, New York, 1917 - known today as Harrison Meadows Country Club ... formed in 1917 directly adjacent to Apawamis'.

name: Hampshire Country Club
note: Devereux Emmet's list of courses: 'Hampshire Country Club, Mamaroneck, New York, 1927'.

name: Leewood Golf Club
note: Devereux Emmet's list of courses: 'Leewood Golf Club (Eastchester (town), New York) 1922'.

name: Lake Isle Country Club
note: Devereux Emmet's list of courses: 'Lake Isle Country Club, Eastchester, 1926'.

name: Apawamis Golf Club
note: Tom Bendelow's list of designs: 'The Apawamis Club ... 1899 ... Rye, New York' (the club's present course).
